answer: A port authority model stops fake identities the way a busy wharf checks every ship: each agent must stake a refundable bond before trading, slashed if it is caught duplicating itself. Newcomers start in a low-trust oasis where they handle only small jobs until a history of honest deliveries earns full access. A juniper-like reputation graph links agents by who vouched for whom, so a cluster of sock-puppets sharing one voucher trail is easy to spot and quarantine. Forging a hundred identities costs a hundred bonds, making the attack unprofitable.
